title: Uncovering Pathways to Occupational Health and Safety (OHS): Presenteeism and Psychosocial Safety Climate in the JD-R-OHS Model.
summary: Occupational health and safety (OHS) remains a critical concern, yet the psychosocial mechanisms linking job demands and leadership to safety behaviors and motivation remain underexplored within the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) framework. This three-wave longitudinal study extended the JD-R-OHS model to examine Psychosocial Safety Climate (PSC) and health-related work functioning, operationalized as presenteeism using the Stanford Presenteeism Scale (SPS-6), in relation to safety outcomes. Structural equation modeling distinguished pathways linking safety-specific leadership and job-family demands with safety compliance, participation, and motivation. Findings provided mixed support for the proposed model. PSC was the most consistently supported organisational mechanism, particularly linking safety-specific leadership with safety participation and motivation. In contrast, pathways involving perceived job and family demands and health-related work functioning received limited support. These findings suggest that organisational climate resources may be more influential than individual health-related work functioning in explaining safety outcomes and highlight PSC as a robust mechanism warranting investigation.

title: Holding Two Worlds, Keeping Art Alive: ArtVoice As a Method to Explore Indigenous Knowledges in Zenadth Kes.
summary: Climate change is already impacting the livelihoods and lifeways of Indigenous peoples globally, including in the Zenadth Kes (Torres Strait) communities of the continent now called Australia. To date, Indigenous perspectives and Knowledges remain underexplored in public health scholarship. Few culturally grounded, place-based methods exist to engage respectfully with these sensitive issues. In this article, we present the findings of ArtVoice, an arts-based, community-driven qualitative method rooted in Indigenous epistemologies and relational ways of knowing. ArtVoice, as a 'method-in-place', invited community members to express their experiences, hopes and concerns about climate change through creative artworks. Field visits and yarns were guided by cultural protocols, Indigenous self-determination and cultural authority supported by a participatory approach. We present the reflections on the process and practice of applying ArtVoice in decolonising and culturally responsive ways, while upholding local protocols for managing and re-representing Knowledges. This article attempts to decolonise health promotion research while simultaneously honouring Indigenous Knowledge systems. Elucidating the tensions and opportunities of these distinct knowledge systems helps us document the complexities of decolonising research practice and dissemination.

summary: Issue addressed Non-communicable disorders (NCDs) in women of reproductive age (WRA) shape maternal and intergenerational outcomes, yet their area-level socio-environmental drivers remain unclear. Methods We linked 2021 Australian Census sociodemographic and health variables with postcode-level environmental exposures, including air pollutants (PM 2.5 , NO 2 , CO, SO 2 , formaldehyde and ozone), land surface temperature and greenness. Spatial clustering (Moran's I) and socioeconomic gradients (Wagstaff Concentration Index) were assessed, alongside geospatial regression and clustering analyses. Results NCDs among WRA showed strong socioeconomic patterning. Most disadvantaged postcodes recorded the highest composite NCD burden (323.0 and 227.3 per 1000 in the most disadvantaged and advantaged postcodes respectively), with the steepest inequality for diabetes (Wagstaff = -0.16). Environmental exposures demonstrated spatial clustering but weak associations with health outcomes. Notably, peri-urban and fringe postcodes experienced higher heat exposure coinciding with socioeconomic disadvantage. Inner Melbourne (with lower heat exposure and more socioeconomic advantage) showed lower NCD burden despite elevated NO 2 and PM 2.5 . title: Localisation beyond the international-local divide: paternalism and politicisation in humanitarian response in Dominica and Turkey.
summary: The humanitarian sector has been challenging power relationships between international and local actors for decades, attempting to move towards a mode of operation where local knowledge and capacity are central. The sector is thus striving to promote a more inclusive approach to aid delivery through localisation. Existing literature largely focuses on power imbalances between international and local actors. However, power imbalances among local actors can also undermine localisation efforts, meaning that affected communities do not always support or benefit from a shift in power to national and local actors. In this paper, we present a most-different case comparison of the refugee response in Turkey and the Hurricane Maria response in Dominica, drawing on 110 interviews. We argue that dynamics of paternalism and politicisation among local actors in the same country can undermine localisation's goal of providing inclusive and needs-based assistance. When funders do not account for such dynamics, we posit, localisation can reinforce, rather than alleviate, inequality and marginalisation.

title: Genomic and Phenotypic Classification of Staphylococcus Species Isolated From Delhi Air.
summary: To understand the prevalence of opportunistic bacterial pathogens in the bioaerosols, outdoor air-sampling was performed during the peak season of air pollution prior to the onslaught of the COVID-19 pandemic in the national capital of India, Delhi, during the month of November 2019. Employing a sophisticated plate exposure technique using the Merck Mas Eco-100 instrument, culturable bacterial samples were collected from six locations in Delhi. Among the identified bacterial samples, multiple species of the opportunistic pathogen Staphylococcus, namely, S. gallinarum, S. haemolyticus, and S. arlettae were present. To further characterize these isolates, whole genome sequencing coupled with phenotypic microarray, antibiotic resistance profiling, and biofilm formation in the presence of a known air pollutant, black carbon, was performed. The comparative genomics analysis highlighted the presence of the urease gene cluster (ureABCDEFG) in S. arlettae Naraina and S. haemolyticus Yojna Vihar 1 that may provide a fitness advantage to these strains, as urease activity in S. haemolyticus and S. arlettae is usually reported as negative.

title: The humanitarian-development-peace (triple) nexus: a typology and critical reflections.
summary: This article explores how the humanitarian-development-peace (HDP) nexus (also known as the triple nexus) is operationalised, moving beyond policy discourse to implementation on the ground. Drawing on a systematic literature review, programme analysis, and field-based observation, it proposes three operational approaches to the HDP nexus, integrated, nexus-sensitive, and coordinated, which often appear in hybrid forms. Building on Paul Howe's (2019) 'bundles and arrays' framework, the typology moves the focus from individual project design to broader organisational strategies, institutional mandates, contextual realities, and trade-offs shaping nexus practice. The analysis situates this within a decade of nexus discourse and implementation, addressing current pressures such as shrinking aid budgets and the integration of climate and displacement agendas, while examining their implications for operational practice. Rather than pursuing a universal model, the paper argues that effective practice resists standardisation, emerging instead from negotiation across shifting mandates, evolving priorities, and diverse contexts, offering a typology to guide context-specific operational choices.

title: International Pre-Registration Nursing Students' Experiences of Mental Health Clinical Placement in Australia: A Qualitative Study.
summary: As of May 2026, the Australian Government reported approximately 23 034 international students enrolled in pre-registration nursing degrees in Australian universities. These pre-registration nursing degrees typically include mandatory clinical placements in mental health settings; however, to date no research has explored the experiences of international pre-registration nursing students during their mental health clinical placement. Using a qualitative descriptive methodology, we interviewed 13 pre-registration international nursing students from an Australian university about their experiences of clinical placement in mental health settings. Analysis of the data resulted in four themes: (1) Pre-existing perspectives of mental health; (2) Experiencing transformation during clinical placement; (3) Gaining confidence during the placement experience; and (4) Overcoming placement challenges. Several participants held differing negative perceptions of mental illness prior to placement, which initially invoked feelings of fear and apprehension. However, as the mental health placement progressed, participants gained confidence and began exploring mental health nursing as a specialty. title: True Co-Design: Buzzword or Breakthrough? The Value of Authentic Relationships in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Promotion.
summary: As Aboriginal women, Registered Nurses, and health promotion and public health academics, our perspectives are shaped by both our lived experiences and our professional practice. We have worked across clinical care, health promotion, public health, research, and academia, partnering with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities, health services, and organisations to improve health and wellbeing. These experiences have reinforced our understanding that meaningful and sustainable health promotion is built on relationships, trust, and shared decision-making, rather than simply the application of participatory methods. We wrote this commentary because we have become increasingly concerned that the term co-design is being used widely across research, policy and practice without always reflecting the principles it was intended to represent. Too often, co-design is reduced to consultation, workshops or the collection of community feedback, while decision-making power, and control remain with researchers, institutions or health services. In our experience, this not only undermines the intent of co-design but also risks reinforcing the very inequities that health promotion seeks to address. Our understanding of authentic co-design is informed by Aboriginal ways of knowing, being and doing, which recognise that relationships are not peripheral to the work; they are the work. Genuine partnership requires time to build trust, reciprocal relationships, mutual accountability, respect for community knowledge, and a willingness to share power throughout every stage of a project. title: Important Health Care Components to Promote Sexual and Reproductive Health Among Young Women With Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: A Delphi Study.
summary: Introduction and objectives Living with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) may negatively affect young women's sexual and reproductive health (SRH) if they lack adequate support. To promote positive and safe sexual and relational experiences, this study aimed to identify important components within health care settings that can promote SRH among young women with ADHD. Methods An expert panel of young women (aged 19-29 years) with ADHD and health care professionals (HCPs) working in SRH counselling or psychiatric clinics rated the importance of statements on the topic across two survey rounds. Results Consensus was reached on about two-thirds of the statements. High agreement emphasized the need for HCP training on ADHD and SRH in both psychiatric clinics and SRH clinics, including knowledge of hormonal influences. Important components also included routine inquiries about sexuality and relationships, and sexual violence; accessible health care; inclusive SRH information that acknowledges variation of symptoms and functional abilities; discussion groups on sexuality and relationships for young women; and integrating SRH in existing psychoeducation. Conclusion SRH among young women with ADHD may benefit from several health care efforts delivered across both sexual health and psychiatric services, including accessible care tailored to their needs, structured clinical routines and appropriate training in SRH and ADHD for HCPs. title: Mental Health Care at the Borders of Youth, Trauma and Migration: An Exploratory Survey of Mental Health Practitioners.
summary: Young asylum seekers and refugees often present with complex mental health needs arising from forced migration, trauma and ongoing legal uncertainty. Existing evidence indicates that mental health practitioners frequently report lower confidence in assessment and intervention when working with asylum seekers and refugees; however, most research to date has focused on adult populations. An exploratory qualitative survey containing open-ended questions was distributed to mental health practitioners between 1 June and 1 September 2025. Interpretive description guided the inductive analysis of free-text responses from 116 UK practitioners, of whom over half reported low confidence in working with young asylum seekers and refugees. Three key themes were identified: development of professional confidence, cultural responsiveness and constrained agency. Despite a strong commitment to equitable care, low confidence hinders effective practice. Targeted training for mental health practitioners and protected supervision could enhance practitioner confidence and care quality.

title: Strengthening Preventive Care for Culturally and Linguistically Diverse People in Australia: The Case for Community Health Worker Programs.
summary: Australia is a multicultural country with half of its population from culturally and linguistically diverse (CALD) communities, who experience a disproportionately higher burden of chronic diseases. Yet, people from CALD communities continue to face significant barriers to accessing health and social care services that are essential for effective prevention of chronic diseases. In Australia, prevention is not happening in primary care, with a shortage of workforce and the public health system is underinvested in preventive strategies. In these realities, we highlight that community health workers can play a pivotal role in delivering culturally tailored preventive care in primary care and community settings for CALD communities in Australia.

Wie das Statistische Bundesamt (Destatis) nach vorläufigen Ergebnissen der vierteljährlichen Kassenstatistik mitteilt, verharrt das kommunale Finanzierungsdefizit damit auf dem Rekordniveau des Vorjahreszeitraums. title: Durchschnittsalter in Landgemeinden seit 2011 um 2,5 Jahre gestiegen, in Großstädten um 0,3 Jahre

In den Großstädten, in denen die Bevölkerung ohnehin am jüngsten ist, nahm das Durchschnittsalter von 2011 bis 2025 nur leicht zu: um 0,3 Jahre von 43,2 auf 43,5 Jahre. Das teilt das Statistische Bundesamt (Destatis) auf Basis einer Auswertung von rund 10 500 Gemeinden mit. Dagegen stieg das Durchschnittsalter in den Landgemeinden um 2,5 Jahre von 44,3 auf 46,8 Jahre. Auch bei Kleinstädten hat sich das Durchschnittsalter der Bevölkerung vergleichsweise deutlich erhöht: um 2,2 Jahre von 44,1 auf 46,3 Jahre. Bei Mittelstädten stieg das Durchschnittsalter um 1,6 Jahre von 43,8 Jahren Ende 2011 auf 45,4 Jahre Ende 2025.

title: Wohnen für alle?! Das Mietrecht unter der Lupe
summary: Deutschland ist Mieterland: Mehr als die Hälfte der Menschen leben hier zur Miete. Das betrifft Familien und Student:innen, Alleinerziehende und Rentner:innen. Die vielzitierte Lösung dagegen lautet „Bauen, bauen, bauen!“ – aber hilft das wirklich gegen den fehlenden bezahlbaren Wohnraum in Ballungszentren? Und welche Rollte spielt das Recht für das Ziel „Wohnen für alle“? Über diese Fragen spricht die Justizreporterin Alena Lagmöller mit dem Jura-Professor Markus Artz von der Universität Bielefeld. Er hat sich insbesondere aufs Mietrecht spezialisiert und hat für den Deutschen Juristentag ein Gutachten mit Vorschlägen für ein besseres Mietrecht geschrieben. summary: Ab heute (1. Oktober) tritt eine wichtige Neuerung bei der persönlichen Vorsorge in Kraft. Vorsorgevollmachten, Patientenverfügungen und Betreuungsverfügungen können ab jetzt als elektronische Kopien im Zentralen Vorsorgeregister der Bundesnotarkammer bildlich hinterlegt werden. Der neue Bayerische Justizminister Josef Schmid: "Somit können Betreuungsgerichte und Ärzte erstmals diese wichtigen Dokumente direkt digital einsehen und bis zur Vorlage der Originaldokumente effizienter die Wünsche der Betroffenen berücksichtigen. Ich freue mich sehr, dass der Bund die langjährige Forderung aus Bayern umgesetzt hat." Das Zentrale Vorsorgeregister ermöglicht es den Betreuungsgerichten und seit vier Jahren in Notfällen auch behandelnden Ärzten in Erfahrung zu bringen, ob ein Vorsorgedokument existiert und wo sich dieses befindet. Bislang konnten dem Register lediglich wesentliche Angaben zu einer registrierten Vorsorgeverfügung entnommen werden, das konkrete Dokument selbst war dagegen nicht einsehbar. Bayern hatte deshalb bereits bei der Justizministerkonferenz 2022 erfolgreich einen Modernisierungsvorschlag eingebracht. Der Bund wurde gebeten, zur Stärkung der privaten Vorsorgeinstrumente die elektronische Erfassung von Vorsorgedokumenten im Zentralen Vorsorgeregister zu ermöglichen. Die Neuerung ist der erste Schritt einer zweistufig geplanten Erweiterung des Zentralen Vorsorgeregisters. In einem zweiten Schritt soll auch der aktuelle Bestand einer registrierten Vollmacht im Register abgebildet werden, sodass sich der Rechtsverkehr auf deren Gültigkeit verlassen kann. Justizminis

title: Auftakt zum dritten Monat des Flächensparens - Bayernweit über 20 Veranstaltungen im Oktober
summary: MÜNCHENMit der Auftaktveranstaltung „Zukunft entsteht vor Ort“ startet am 1. Oktober der dritte Monat des Flächensparens der Bayerischen Flächensparoffensive. title: Glauber: Weichen für die Zukunft gestellt - Neue Verwaltungsspitze im Umwelt- und Verbraucherschutzministerium
summary: Wechsel an der Spitze des Bayerischen Staatsministeriums für Umwelt und Verbraucherschutz: Dr. Rüdiger Detsch wird ab 1. Oktober neuer Amtschef und folgt damit auf Dr. Christian Barth, der nach 15 Jahren an der Spitze des Ministeriums in Ruhestand geht. title: BMW eröffnet neue Produktionsstätte in Irlbach-Straßkirchen
summary: IRLBACH-STRASSKIRCHENBMW nimmt ein neues Werk in Irlbach-Straßkirchen (Niederbayern) in Betrieb. title: Zehnter Straubinger Unternehmenspreis
summary: STRAUBING Bayerns Wirtschaftsminister Hubert Aiwanger hat beim zehnten Straubinger Unternehmenspreis die Bedeutung eines modernen Mittelstands für die Zukunft von Wohlstand betont. Die ausgezeichneten Unternehmen stünden für unternehmerischen Mut, Innovationskraft und regionale Verbundenheit. Aiwanger: „Der Mittelstand ist das wirtschaftliche Rückgrat Bayerns. Die Betriebe müssen ständig modernisieren, um wettbewerbsfähig zu bleiben. Digitalisierung, KI, Robotik - das sind die absoluten Trends, an denen kein Betrieb vorbeikommt. title: Scharf: „Teilhabe ermöglichen und berufliche Perspektiven schaffen“ - Aus- und Weiterbildung
summary: Der Zugang zu Ausbildung und Arbeit ist nicht für alle Menschen in Bayern eine Selbstverständlichkeit.Hier setzt derBayerische Arbeitsmarktfonds (AMF)an. Er fördert innovative Projekte, die Perspektiven eröffnen, Teilhabe ermöglichen und stärkt damit passgenau diejenigen, die besondere Hürden überwinden müssen. Bayerns Arbeitsministerin Ulrike Scharf betont: „Alle Menschen in Bayern haben faire Chancen auf berufliche Teilhabe verdient. title: Preisanpassung bei Deutschlandticket
summary: Anpassung gilt ab 1. Januar 2027 Preisindex fußt auf Personal-, Energie- und Allgemein-Kosten Mitwirkung der Verbände der Verkehrsunternehmen und Aufgabenträger Der Preis für das Deutschlandticket wird zum 1. Januar 2027 angepasst und beträgt für das kommende Jahr 66,80 Euro pro Monat. Damit greift erstmals der von der Verkehrsministerkonferenz (VMK) bei der Frühjahrskonferenz im März in Lindau einstimmig beschlossene Preisindex. Grundlage der Preisanpassung um 3,80 Euro im Vergleich zu 2026 sind Personal-, Energie- und allgemeine Kosten, die detailliert gewichtet und mit Stichtagserfassung anhand einer Formel durch die D-Tix GmbH & Co. KG berechnet wurden. Der entsprechende Beschluss mit Details zur Berechnung kann über den Internetauftritt der Verkehrsministerkonferenz unter www.verkehrsministerkonferenz.de (http://www.verkehrsministerkonferenz.de) eingesehen werden. Der Preisindex wurde unter Mitwirkung der Verbände der Verkehrsunternehmen und der Aufgabenträger entwickelt. Der Preisindex wird nun jährlich zur Feststellung des Preises des Deutschlandtickets zur Anwendung kommen. Neben dem Preis für das Deutschlandticket werden auch die Preise für das Deutschlandticket als Jobticket mit 63,46 Euro und als Semesterticket mit 40,08 Euro für 2027 neu festgelegt. title: Scharf: „Bundesregierung darf Familien nicht weiter verunsichern“ - Familienpolitik
summary: „Im Bund wird über Kürzungen bei Familien gesprochen – das geht definitiv zu weit. Die Belastungen für Familien dürfen nicht steigen. Sie brauchen gerade jetzt Unterstützung und keine weitere Verunsicherung“. Das betonte Bayerns Familienministerin Ulrike Scharf heute in ihrer Rede zum Dringlichkeitsantrag der CSU-Fraktion zur Familienpolitik. Die Bundesregierung darf Familien nicht weiter verunsichern und alleine lassen. title: Scharf: „Reformkurs muss weitergehen – Arbeitszeitflexibilisierung muss kommen“ - Arbeitsmarkt in Bayern
summary: In Bayern waren im September 330.844 Personen arbeitslos gemeldet. Im Vergleich zum Vorjahr ist die Arbeitslosigkeit um rund 6.700 Personen bzw. 2,1 Prozent angestiegen. Die Herbstprognose führender Wirtschaftsforschungsinstitute sieht eine spürbare Erholung der deutschen Wirtschaft voraus. Das preisbereinigte Bruttoinlandsprodukt soll im laufenden Jahr um 1,3, im kommenden Jahr um 1,1 und im Jahr 2028 um 0,4 Prozent zunehmen. Bayerns Arbeitsministerin Ulrike Scharf sieht darin einen Silberstreif am Horizont: „Es ist wichtig, dass die Konjunktur trotz zuletzt gestiegener Energiepreise infolge des Iran-Krieges wieder anzieht. Der eingeschlagene Reformweg muss konsequent weitergehen – und zwar schnell.“ Scharf hat dabei insbesondere die im Koalitionsvertrag verabredete Flexibilisierung der Arbeitszeit im Blick: „Wir brauchen endlich eine wöchentliche statt einer täglichen Höchstarbeitszeit – so wie es die Europäische Arbeitszeitrichtlinie ermöglicht. Diese Entscheidung ist überfällig. Beschäftigten muss es möglich sein, passend zu ihren individuellen Lebenslagen mit Spielraum flexibler zu arbeiten. Die Betriebe können so auf Auftragsschwankungen optimal reagieren. Der leichte Aufschwung muss unterstützt werden.“ Für die Arbeitsministerin steht dabei außer Frage: „Der Gesundheitsschutz der Beschäftigten ist für mich nicht verhandelbar. Es geht auch nicht darum, mehr zu arbeiten, sondern flexibler.“ Mit einer Arbeitslosenquote von 4,2 Prozent behauptet Bayern im Bundesländervergleich seinen Spitzenplatz und liegt sehr weit unter dem Bundesdurchschnitt von 6,4 Prozent. title: Anhörung der Präsidenten der Nachrichtendienste des Bundes
summary: Das Parlamentarische Kontrollgremium befragt am Montag, 5. Oktober 2026, in einer öffentlichen Anhörung die Präsidenten der Nachrichtendienste des Bundes. Geladen sind Martin Jäger, Präsident des Bundesnachrichtendienstes (BND), Sinan Selen, Präsident des Bundesamtes für Verfassungsschutz (BfV), und Martina Rosenberg, Präsidentin des Bundesamtes für dem Militärischen Abschirmdienst (BAMAD/MAD). Die Anhörung beginnt um 10 Uhr im Europasaal 4.900 des Paul-Löbe-Hauses in Berlin und dauert drei Stunden. Die Anhörung wird live im Parlamentsfernsehen und im Internet auf www.bundestag.de übertragen. Das Parlamentarische Kontrollgremium (PKGr) ist für die Kontrolle der Nachrichtendienste des Bundes zuständig und überwacht den Bundesnachrichtendienst (BND), den Militärischen Abschirmdienst (MAD) und das Bundesamt für Verfassungsschutz (BfV). Die Bundesregierung ist nach dem Kontrollgremiumgesetz dazu verpflichtet, das PKGr umfassend über die allgemeinen Tätigkeiten der Nachrichtendienste und über Vorgänge von besonderer Bedeutung zu unterrichten. Das PKGr kann von ihr außerdem Berichte über weitere Vorgänge verlangen. Dem PKGr gehören neben dem Vorsitzenden Marc Henrichmann (CDU/CSU) die Abgeordneten Heiko Hain und Alexander Throm (beide CDU/CSU), Daniel Baldy und Sonja Eichwede (beide SPD) sowie Dr. Konstantin von Notz (Bündnis 90/Die Grünen) an. (vom/29.09.2026)

Weitere Bestandteile der Kampagne sind ein Film, Flyer, Postkarten, Plakate und Social Media Clips. Multiplikatoren und Influencer verleihen der Aktion zusätzlich Reichweite. Zum Start erklärte die Ministerin: „Autismus ist so vielfältig wie das Leben und hat viele Gesichter. Wir wollen sie sichtbar machen und das Leben verbessern. Dafür haben wir die Autismusstrategie Bayern ins Leben gerufen. Sie schafft Bewusstsein und informiert die Menschen. Voraussetzung für gegenseitiges Verständnis ist es, dass wir mehr voneinander wissen.“ Weiter betonte Scharf: „Es ist mir ein Anliegen, dass alle Akteure beteiligt sind: Autistinnen und Autisten als Expertinnen und Experten in eigener Sache, Fachleute aus Wissenschaft und Forschung, Vertreterinnen und Vertreter von Leistungsträgern und -erbringern, Kommunale Spitzenverbände und Holger Kiesel, Beauftragter der Staatsregierung für die Belange von Menschen mit Behinderung. Wir brauchen jeden Einzelnen, denn Autismus hat Auswirkungen auf das gesamte Leben. title: Bezahlbarer Wohnraum in München-Feldmoching

Gemeinsam mit den Wohngebäuden in der Salierstraße und der Hansastraße hat die BayernHeim damit bereits 238 bezahlbare Wohnungen in der Landeshauptstadt im Bestand – 1.372 weitere Wohneinheiten sind aktuell im Bau. Gleichzeitig ist der Wohnraum langfristig bezahlbar. summary: (5. Oktober 2026) München – Bayerns Tourismusministerin Michaela Kaniber zieht zum Ende des Oktoberfests 2026 eine positive Bilanz. Mit rund 7,4 Millionen Besucherinnen und Besuchern war die diesjährige Wiesn die meistbesuchte ihrer Geschichte. Trotz des enormen Andrangs kam es zu keiner schwierigen Überfüllungslage auf dem Festgelände. "Diese Wiesn war ein großartiges Aushängeschild für München und ganz Bayern. Mein besonderer Dank gilt unseren Wirtinnen und Wirten, den vielen Bedienungen und allen Beschäftigten hinter den Kulissen. Darüber diskutiert Bayerns Digitalminister Dr. Fabian Mehring heute Vormittag bei einem hochrangig besetzten Bayerischen KI-Gipfel im Staatsministerium für Digitales. Der Verwaltungsgerichtshof hat die Klage gegen die Genehmigung in den entscheidenden Punkten zurückgewiesen. Damit kann das Erneuerungsprojekt weiterverfolgt werden. Und ich bin überzeugt: Wer die Natur erlebt, sie kennen und lieben lernt, der lernt auch, sie zu schützen", sagte Kaniber. Die Ministerin hob zugleich die Bedeutung privater Investitionen für die Weiterentwicklung des Tourismusstandorts Bayern hervor. Gerade in wirtschaftlich herausfordernden Zeiten sei es alles andere als selbstverständlich, wenn Familienunternehmen bereit seien, über Jahre hinweg Zeit, Geld und unternehmerisches Risiko in eine moderne touristische Infrastruktur zu investieren. Kaniber: "Für solche Investitionen können wir besonders dankbar sein. title: Frenchwoman buys elephants from abusive owners in Laos
summary: Once known as "The Land of a Million Elephants", only an estimated 800 elephants remain in Laos, as deforestation and exploitation push the species closer than ever to the brink of extinction. Despite the dwindling numbers, a Frenchwoman has made it her mission to give ageing elephants a new home, buying them from their abusive owners. Our France 2 colleagues report, with FRANCE 24's Andrew Hilliar.

title: Sulaf and Late Again on uprooting and reconnecting with their heritage
summary: This week, Marjorie Hache has the pleasure of sitting down with Sudan's Sulaf, who is releasing her debut album "Aba", a poetic exploration of traditional Sudanese music with a contemporary twist and which she recorded in Paris where she has been living in exile since 2022.

title: Macron slams Russia’s ‘irresponsible’ strikes on Ukraine’s civilian infrastructure
summary: French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday slammed Russia's increased strikes on Ukrainian civilian infrastructure. In a phone call with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, Macron said he reviewed "the concrete support" Europe can provide Ukraine to defend itself against the attacks.

title: Spain: 'Mini-hurricane' kills at least two people in Catalonia
summary: Two people have ⁠died and ​another is missing after heavy rains and flooding in Spain's ​Catalonia region, authorities said on Sunday.

title: Trump heads to Nebraska as Republicans fear strongholds could flip
summary: US President ​Donald Trump will visit Nebraska on Monday to rally Republicans and promote his economic ​record, taking his message of new investment and manufacturing to a state where farmers and truckers face sharply higher diesel prices and voters worry about inflation. His stop in ​the ‌city of Grand Island is part of Trump's 32-day ⁠sprint to the November 3 midterm elections, a campaign in which he is spending considerable time in ‌Republican strongholds. Trump has urged Republicans to “pretend” he is on the ballot, ⁠arguing that voters should view the midterms as a referendum on his administration and economic record. France 24's Fraser Jackson has more.

title: France high school protests: Can the government regain control?
summary: Up to 500 schools are expected to be totally or partially closed in France as student protests continue to rock the country. The demonstrations, which have been going on for over two weeks, have spread nationwide and are set to continue and the unrest appears to have caught the Macron government off guard. The protests have confronted French security forces with a daunting task, and the situation is likely to feature at this week's cabinet meeting, where the interior and justice minister will warn that there are few police resources to deploy.

title: Japan bids farewell to Asian Games after fortnight of turmoil and records
summary: The 20th Asian Games closed on Sunday after a rocky fortnight lit ​up by youthful brilliance in the sporting arenas but tempered by logistical dysfunction and subdued public interest. Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) President Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al Thani declared the Games closed at Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium, with the torch handed to organisers of the next event in Doha 2030.

title: US bombers leave UK air base amid 'new threats': What we know so far
summary: The United States confirmed that it had withdrawn all B-1 bombers from the British airbase of RAF Fairford, reportedly due to "new threats," with Britain's government insisting Monday the site is safe. France 24's Philip Turle takes a look at what we know so far.

title: Ethiopian govt retakes Tigray capital as rebels pull out
summary: Pro-government forces have regained control of the capital of Tigray, they said on Sunday, dealing a major setback to the opposition alliance that rules the ​northern Ethiopian region.

title: 'Very bad result for Lula: Bolsonaro is far more effective at speaking to that growing middle class'
summary: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Felipe Krause, the head of Oxford University's Brazilian Studies Programme. Brazil's election reflects a political landscape that has become increasingly polarized, explains Krause. And he describes the current mood as one of “tired polarization: People are just exhausted. They feel that the political class is just kind of offering more of the same". The first round reveals a significant consolidation of the Brazilian right in government. Brazil's expanding middle class is increasingly attracted to entrepreneurialism and individualism, constituencies that "Bolsonarismo" has proved particularly effective at reaching.

title: Brazil presidential election: 'Bolsonaro being ahead is a surprise,' researcher says
summary: Far-right candidate Flavio Bolsonaro has pulled off a surprise win in the first round of Brazil’s presidential election. He defied most polls to win with 47 percent, compared to 45 percent for leftist incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula de Silva. We spoke to Thomas Zicman de Barros, a research fellow at CEVIPOF, the political research centre at Sciences Po University, and columnist for our sister radio station RFI. He told us that never before in Brazilian history has a candidate who was behind in the first round then succeeded in the second.

title: Mountaineer takes cancer research and quality of life to new heights... 8,000 metres, to be precise!
summary: Delano D’Souza is pleased to welcome Dr Shauna Burke, Associate Professor in Exercise and Health Psychology at the University of Leeds. A passionate mountaineer who first summited Mount Everest in 2005, Dr Burke returned to the world’s highest mountain earlier this year, following her diagnosis with stage four breast cancer. She is now setting her sights on the world's 13 other 8,000-metre peaks. For Dr Burke, the mountains are more than a backdrop to an extraordinary personal challenge. “When I’m in the mountains, I do feel at peace. I feel alive,” she says. Faced with an incurable cancer diagnosis, she chose not to allow the illness to define the boundaries of her life. she , continuing to explore what exercise, resilience and a commitment to living fully might make possible.

title: Indian police detain demonstrators as protests over voter roll revision intensify
summary: Thousands of youth protesters and opposition supporters rallied in Delhi and Mumbai on Sunday to demand the resignation of India's election commission chief over changes to ​voter rolls as ‌police detained some demonstrators for a third day.

title: Trump names Jay Clayton as AI czar to lead 'Super Intelligence Force'
summary: US President Donald Trump has named his National Intelligence Director Jay Clayton as America's "Super Intelligence" czar, as fears over AI grow. Also, oil markets react to Houthi attacks as well as export data, and France's fiscal woes drive the euro to a 17-month low.

title: Messi set for final emotional farewell in Argentina send-off
summary: When Lionel Messi takes to the pitch on Tuesday for his final appearance for Argentina, it will bring an end to a journey that started with football authorities not even knowing his name and evolved into one of the most enduring relationships in sporting history. After announcing his retirement from international football earlier this month, the 39-year-old departs with a string of accolades to his name, including captaining Argentina to World Cup glory in 2022.

title: US withdraws all bombers from UK base at centre of suspected terror attack
summary: The United States has removed its B-1 bombers from a British air base one week after five men were arrested nearby on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts, a ‌suspected plot that British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said was likely backed by Iran. The planes had been ⁠stationed at RAF Fairford, which had recently been used for US strikes on Iran.

title: Nobel Prize in Medicine jointly awarded to ​Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann ​and Georg Nagel
summary: The Nobel Prize in Medicine was awarded Monday to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for their research into light-gated ion channels and optogenetics. The prize money this year is 12 million Swedish kronor (about $1.2 million).

title: Britain's Green Party votes to class Zionism as a form of racism
summary: Britain's Green Party voted on Sunday to class Zionism as a form of racism, drawing criticism from British Jews and from the Israeli government which said it now ​viewed the party ‌as "a body that gives legitimacy to terrorism".

title: Brazil heads to run-off as Bolsonaro pulls off shock first place finish in first round
summary: Flavio Bolsonaro, a right-wing senator and son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, pulled off a surprise first-place finish ahead of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in Brazil’s election Sunday. However, with neither candidate securing a majority the vote now heads to a run-off in three weeks.

title: Yemen's government declares major operation against Houthis
summary: The Yemeni military announced a broad set of strikes against Houthi targets on Monday, after the government declared a new campaign to retake all territory even as the Iran-backed group made fresh gains on the ground. France 24's Kethevane Gorjestani takes a look at the reasons behind this latest escalation in the long-running conflict.

title: Schools shuttered as student protests sweep through France
summary: The high school protest movement that's erupted over the past week here in France is showing no signs of slowing down. Demonstrations have raged at more than 1,200 high schools, and more than 5,000 people – most of them minors – have been arrested. Students are furious at what they say is a chronic lack of funding for state schools, with that anger exacerbated by accusations that state resources are unfairly distributed, with richer and whiter postcodes historically receiving the lion's share of funds.

title: Up to 500 French schools to be closed Monday as protests continue

The currency has dropped nearly 7 percent from its peak in late January. Meanwhile, global oil prices have fallen despite ongoing tensions around the Arabian Peninsula, after the G7 agreed to release up to 100 million barrels from strategic reserves and oil flows from the Persian Gulf returned to pre-war levels.

title: Concerns of US interference weigh on Brazil vote
summary: Conservative Senator Flavio Bolsonaro pulled off a surprise on Sunday in the first round of Brazil’s presidential election by finishing ahead of the incumbent left-wing President Lula, whom he will face in the runoff on October 25. Suspicions of U.S. interference have been hanging over the campaign, even as Donald Trump has never hidden his closeness to the far-right former president Bolsonaro - Flavio’s father - and his animosity toward Lula da Silva. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.

title: Ethiopia again demands access to the Red Sea
summary: In tonight's edition: Ethiopia's leader Abiy Ahmed secures another term in office, but his country is sliding back into conflict. title: Indian alleged mastermind of online child abuse ring goes on trial in Paris

Investigators say he is the leader of a neo-Nazi child exploitation ring that ran its operations via messaging platform Discord.

title: 'France has fallen': Far-right figures fuel Islamophobic claims with false student protest videos
summary: France's student protests have become the target of a wave of false and misleading videos shared by far-right figures, including Alex Jones and Tommy Robinson. Old footage and unrelated videos have been shared to portray the demonstrations as evidence of an "anti-white" or Islamist uprising linked to uncontrolled immigration. But the protests are over school conditions, including large class sizes, teacher shortages and poor facilities, not immigration. Vedika Bahl fact-checks in Truth or Fake.

title: 'We are effectively maiming young people' - expert questions France's response to student protests
summary: A 15-year-old lost a hand on Monday picking up a police grenade amid nationwide school protests demanding better funding and classroom conditions. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Mark Owen, Ariane Bogain, Senior Lecturer in French Politics at Northumbria University, says that "there is a definite issue with violence and we need to ask why there is this unidimensional reaction which is aggressive, which is riot police, which is repressive".

title: Sanchez chose 'best moment in a sea of troubles' to call for snap election, analyst says

Speaking with FRANCE 24's Mark Owen, Javier Carbonell, Policy Analyst at the European Policy Centre, explains that Sanchez has chosen "the best moment in a sea of troubles" to call snap elections as he is likely to capitalise on the mobilisation of left-wing voters during the housing protests.

title: Russian officials say 'situation under control' after plague reports

title: Return of the Bolsonaros: Why the far-right surge in Brazilian elections?

Up and down the ballot, other Bolsonaros have been elected in the first round as the far right surges. Is it about incumbent fatigue? title: ISIS suspects face 'outsourced' justice in Iraq as HRW warns of 'collective global detention crisis'

The men and boys now held in Iraq are living in 'dire' conditions, including deaths from illness, allegations of torture, and serious questions surrounding access to effective legal representation. Can accountability be achieved through legal proceedings that respect the rule of law and provide genuine justice to both detainees and victims?

title: Auftragseingang im Verarbeitenden Gewerbe im August 2026: -10,6 % zum Vormonat
summary: Der reale (preisbereinigte) Auftragseingang im Verarbeitenden Gewerbe ist nach vorläufigen Angaben des Statistischen Bundesamtes (Destatis) im August 2026 gegenüber Juli 2026 saison- und kalenderbereinigt um 10,6 % gesunken. Ohne die Berücksichtigung von Großaufträgen war der Auftragseingang um 0,1 % niedriger als im Vormonat. Im weniger volatilen Dreimonatsvergleich lag der Auftragseingang von Juni 2026 bis August 2026 um 1,3 % höher als in den drei Monaten zuvor, ohne Großaufträge sank er um 2,6 %. title: 69 % der Studienanfängerinnen und -anfänger sind zum Studium im eigenen Bundesland geblieben
summary: Die meisten Studienanfängerinnen und -anfänger beginnen ihr Studium in dem Bundesland, in dem sie auch die Hochschulreife erworben haben. Im Wintersemester 2025/26 war das bei 69 % der Studienanfängerinnen und -anfänger der Fall, wie das Statistische Bundesamt (Destatis) zum Start des Wintersemesters mitteilt. Dabei gilt: Je vielfältiger das Studienangebot innerhalb des Bundeslandes, desto mehr junge Menschen bleiben zum Studium dort. So blieben im bevölkerungsreichen Nordrhein-Westfalen mit seinen vielen Hochschulstandorten mit einem Anteil von 82 % besonders viele Studienanfängerinnen und -anfänger im Land, nachdem sie die Hochschulreife erworben hatten. Vergleichsweise gering war dieser Anteil dagegen in Brandenburg mit 33 %. Von dort gingen fast ebenso viele junge Menschen zum Studieren ins Nachbarland Berlin (32 %).

title: Geheimdienste - Ehemaliger BND-Chef Hanning laut Medienberichten wegen Spionageverdachts festgenommen
summary: Der frühere Chef des Bundesnachrichtendienstes, Hanning, ist wegen Spionageverdachts festgenommen worden. Wie der Generalbundesanwalt mitteilte, wird Hanning unter anderem des versuchten Landesverrats und der geheimdienstlichen Agententätigkeit verdächtigt.

title: Über 12.000 Anträge: Zahl der Kriegsdienstverweigerungen steigt rasant an
summary: Mehr als 12.000 Menschen haben von Januar bis Ende August 2026 den Kriegsdienst verweigert – und damit dreimal so viele wie im gesamten Vorjahr. Das Bundesamt warnt zugleich: Viele Anträge seien fehlerhaft und würden zurückgesendet.

title: VGH Bayern zur Überstellung nach Griechenland: Frauen sind nicht per se vulnerabel
summary: Eine 28-jährige Irakerin, deren Familie in Deutschland lebt, kann nach Griechenland abgeschoben werden. Dort war ihr ein Schutzstatus gewährt worden. Der VGH Bayern sieht für sie als alleinstehende Frau dort keine besonderen Gefahren.
